speaker: Penny
teaser: Her husband says she never listens. She says he mumbles.
hello: Hi! Penny Natter. My husband says I never listen. I say he mumbles.
So here I am. Test me, and I'll take the results home and frame them.

which_ear.say: Both the same, I think. I hear everything. When I want to.

onset.say: He says it's been years. Nothing sudden. I'd have noticed. Probably.

ringing.say: No ringing. Just my phone, all day long.

red_flags.say: No pain, no gunk, no spinning. My ears feel totally fine.

noise.say: Earbuds on the train, every day. Loud enough to drown out the train. Is that bad?

ear_history.say: Never had an ear infection. Never even had my ears looked at.

family.say: Nope. Grandma's ninety-six and hears gossip through walls.
family.note: No hearing loss in the family

health.say: Healthy as a horse. No medicines. A LOT of coffee.

aids.say: Never! I'm only here to prove him wrong.

say: Parties and busy coffee shops. Everyone talks at once, so I just smile and nod.
At home he talks from the kitchen over the dishwasher. I hear him... later.
Recording my podcast? Perfect. Headphones on, one voice at a time.
hardest.note: Trouble: parties, coffee shops, kitchen talk

right.caption: Penny's RIGHT ear: a clean canal, a shiny pearly eardrum.

left.caption: Penny's LEFT ear: just the same. Healthy and clear.

decision_lines.fit: Hearing aids for normal hearing? Every tone was 25 or better. They'd only make things louder.
decision_lines.refer: Refer for what? Normal hearing, healthy eardrums, no red flags. No doctor needed.
decision_lines.today: No emergency here: nothing sudden, no pain, and normal hearing in both ears.
decision_lines.clear: Normal hearing in both ears! No aids needed. Distance is her trouble at home, not her ears.

why.prompt: Why does Penny need no hearing aids?
options: Every tone was 25 dB or better in both ears.
Right! 25 dB or better is a common adult normal. WHO's normal: a better-ear average under 20.
She is too young for hearing aids.
Age doesn't decide. Children wear hearing aids too. The chart decides.
Her tympanograms were both type A.
Type A means the eardrum moves well. It can't tell how well she hears.
Her husband admitted that he mumbles.
Wishful thinking! It's her chart that clears her: 25 or better everywhere.

debrief: Normal hearing is good news, not a wasted visit. Now there's a baseline for later.
Talking from another room fails for everyone. Face each other, get attention first.
Normal tones, yet parties are hard? Add a speech-in-noise test: it shows how she copes with chatter.
And those loud earbuds: keep them at half volume, with breaks. Damaged hearing doesn't grow back.
goodbye: So I DO hear him. I just wasn't listening. Please don't put that in writing.
Half volume on the train. Got it. Bye, Hoot!

headlines.S: WIFE'S EARS PERFECT; HUSBAND TOLD TO STOP MUMBLING
headlines.A: PENNY PASSES WITH FLYING COLOURS; BASELINE FILED
headlines.B: NORMAL EARS CONFIRMED, A FEW STAMPS WANDERED
headlines.C: PENNY'S EARS FINE, CLINIC'S STAMPING LESS SO
headlines.Do-over: HEARING CHECK HEARD BUT NOT LISTENED TO

subheads.S: Normal hearing in both ears, no red flags. No hearing aids: talk face to face, test speech in noise.
subheads.A: 25 dB or better everywhere means normal. Talk face to face; test speech in noise.
subheads.B: Normal hearing still needs a full check. Look, ask, then test.
subheads.C: Normal means 25 dB or better at every pitch. Check every tone.
subheads.Do-over: Penny will be back. So will her husband, mumbling.
